title: One-Pot Turkey, Spinach & Tomato Rice
description: Ground turkey, rice, tomatoes, and spinach cook in one pan for a simple weeknight dinner with familiar grocery-store ingredients.
substitutions: Use ground chicken instead of turkey.
Use 1 cup thawed frozen spinach, squeezed dry, instead of fresh spinach.
Use vegetable broth if that is what you have.

cookSteps.text: Put 1 pound ground turkey in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat. Cook 5–7 minutes, breaking it into small pieces, until no pink remains.
Stir in 1 cup white rice, 1 can diced tomatoes with their juices, 1 3/4 cups chicken broth, and 1 teaspoon garlic powder. Bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer about 18 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Stir in 2 cups baby spinach until wilted. Sprinkle with up to 1/2 cup shredded cheese if using, cover for 1 minute to melt, then serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat until steaming hot, adding a tablespoon or two of water if the rice seems dry.

title: Ham, Cabbage & Cheddar Quesadillas
description: Thin cabbage, deli ham, and cheddar make crisp skillet quesadillas that turn inexpensive staples into a fast meal.
substitutions: Use deli turkey instead of ham.
Use bagged coleslaw mix instead of shredded cabbage.
Use Monterey Jack or mozzarella instead of cheddar.

cookSteps.text: Divide 4 ounces chopped ham, 1 cup very thinly shredded cabbage, and 1 cup shredded cheddar over 2 tortillas. Spread with up to 2 tablespoons mustard if using, then top with the remaining 2 tortillas.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat with 1 teaspoon butter or oil if using. Cook each quesadilla 3–4 minutes on the first side, until golden.
Flip carefully and cook 2–3 minutes more, until the second side is crisp and the cheese is melted.
Rest 1 minute, cut into wedges, and serve.

storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate cooked quesadillas up to 2 days and re-crisp in a dry skillet or toaster oven.

title: Leftover Chicken, Broccoli & Rice Cakes
description: Cooked rice, leftover chicken, and broccoli become crisp little skillet cakes for an easy food-rescue meal.
substitutions: Use cooked turkey instead of chicken.
Use peas or finely chopped cooked mixed vegetables instead of broccoli.
Use breadcrumbs instead of flour if the mixture needs help holding together.

steps.text: Mix and shape the rice cakes.

cookSteps.text: Mix 1 1/2 cups cold cooked rice, 1 cup chopped cooked chicken, 1 cup chopped cooked broccoli, 1 egg, 1/2 cup shredded cheddar, and 2 tablespoons flour in a bowl. Press into 6 small firm patties.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the patties and cook 4–5 minutes, until the bottoms are golden and the cakes hold together.
Flip carefully and cook another 3–4 minutes, until crisp and hot through.
Serve hot. If a cake feels fragile, let it sit in the skillet another minute before moving it.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days, provided the original chicken and rice were still within their safe refrigerated storage window. Reheat until steaming hot.

title: Small-Batch Chocolate Applesauce Mug Cakes
description: Two soft chocolate cakes use applesauce for moisture and cook quickly in the microwave when you want something sweet without a full batch.
substitutions: Use vanilla yogurt instead of applesauce.
Use any milk you normally keep on hand.
Skip the chocolate chips or use a spoonful of peanut butter in the center instead.

steps.text: Microwave the cakes one at a time.

cookSteps.text: Mix 1/2 cup flour, 3 tablespoons sugar, 2 tablespoons cocoa powder, and 1/2 teaspoon baking powder in a small bowl.
Stir in 1/3 cup applesauce, 1/4 cup milk, and 1 tablespoon oil or melted butter just until smooth. Fold in 2 tablespoons chocolate chips if using.
Divide the batter between 2 microwave-safe mugs. Microwave one mug at a time for 60–90 seconds, until the top looks set but still soft. Microwave ovens vary, so start with 60 seconds.
Let each cake stand 2 minutes before eating; the mug and cake will be hot.

storage: Best eaten right away. If needed, cover and refrigerate up to 1 day, then warm briefly before serving.
